research-team.name: Dr. Jessie Barrot
research-team.testimonial: HealthPH transforms social media data into actionable insights for proactive disease surveillance and a healthier tomorrow.

research-team.name: Dr. Arnold Eniego
research-team.testimonial: HealthPH is a game-changer in disease surveillance. It uses innovative approaches to improve public health, ultimately contributing to nation-building and a better quality of life for all.

research-team.name: Avonn Nova
research-team.position: College Dean, College of Computing and Information Technologies
research-team.testimonial: E-governance and social media integration enable us to tap into real-time data streams, providing a dynamic and responsive approach to managing public health crises.

research-team.name: Dr. Mideth Abisado
research-team.testimonial: Our mission with HealthPH is to weave advanced technology into the fabric of our public health system, ensuring the well-being of every Filipino and preserving the legacy of our diverse languages.

research-team.name: Ramon Rodriguez
research-team.testimonial: The integration of machine learning with social media data analysis has the potential to transform public health surveillance by providing more granular and immediate insights into disease spread and public sentiment.

research-team.name: Joseph Marvin Imperial
research-team.testimonial: I envision HealthPH to be one of the first initiatives for open research where artifacts, findings, code, data, and resources are openly available to the public and adjacent research communities for consumption, dissemination, and advancement of scientific progress in Health x AI.

research-team.name: Bernie Fabito
research-team.testimonial: HealthPH in the near future will leverage the way we listen and pinpoint emerging diseases through social media.

research-team.name: Emeliza Yabut
research-team.testimonial: The utilization of social media for disease surveillance in the Philippines bridges gaps in conventional data collection, offering a comprehensive view of public health dynamics.

research-team.name: Marilen Pacis
research-team.testimonial: The use of social media data in disease surveillance empowers the Philippines to enhance public health monitoring and response efforts, especially in remote or underserved areas.

research-team.name: Dr. Maria Luisa Bautista
research-team.testimonial: Social media analytics can complement traditional surveillance methods, providing a more comperehensive picture of disease activity.

research-team.name: John Carlo Aspiras
research-team.testimonial: A graduate of Bachelor of Science in Business Administration Major in Marketing Management. He has experience in administrative support and research assistance, with strong interpersonal and communication skills, as well as experience in documentation, data analysis, and time management. In his previous work, he was recognized twice as the most competitive employee. Also, he is detail-oriented and adaptable, and always eager to learn and contribute his best, especially in a fast-paced environment.

research-team.name: Maria Christel J. Albay
research-team.testimonial: Ms. Albay is a Finance and Administrative Staff under a DOST-NICER Project 1: HealthPH+, where she supports budget monitoring, financial documentation, and the preparation of financial reports. She ensures proper fund utilization and contributes to efficient project implementation through accurate and organized accounting practices. She earned her Bachelor of Science in Railway Engineering (BSRE) from Polytechnic University of the Philippines-Manila (PUP-Manila). She is committed to working with integrity, excellence, and accountability in all responsibilities entrusted to her. She values discipline, continuous learning, teamwork, and service to the community. Her competencies include budget monitoring, financial reporting, documentation management, office coordination, and strong organizational skills. Outside of her professional responsibilities, she enjoys learning new skills and engaging in activities that foster personal growth.

research-team.name: Angelo Daniel A. Dela Paz
research-team.testimonial: Angelo is a data scientist and incoming MS Data Science student at California State University, Northridge. He completed his Bachelor's degree in Computer Science at the University of Santo Tomas, where he developed a strong interest in machine learning and data analysis. His work focuses on areas such as computer vision, natural language processing, and classification models, primarily using Python and widely used machine learning libraries. He enjoys building and experimenting with models while exploring how data can be used to better understand complex problems.

research-team.name: William Harvey C. Araza
research-team.testimonial: Mr. William Harvey Araza is a Junior Mobile Developer under the DOST-NICER Project 1: HealthPH+. In this role, he is responsible for designing and developing a mobile application for symptom reporting that supports multiple Philippine languages and ensures accessibility for diverse user groups. He holds a Bachelor of Science in Information Technology from the Technological Institute of the Philippines-Quezon City. His professional interests focus on mobile application development and data science, where he explores innovative ways to create efficient, user-centered digital solutions. Through his work, he contributes to the development and implementation of technology-driven projects that support research, development, and institutional initiatives. He continues to enhance his expertise in modern mobile technologies and data analytics, aiming to leverage these fields to build impactful applications and data-driven systems. His work reflects a commitment to continuous learning, technological innovation, and contributing to the advancement of digital transformation in academic and research environments.

research-team.name: Denisse Joy C. Arawag
research-team.testimonial: I have completed a Diploma in Information Communication Technology and a Bachelor of Science in Information Technology. I have experience in web development and AI data annotation, working on systems that support data processing and digital solutions. I am particularly interested in designing and developing management systems that automate manual tasks, improve workflow efficiency, and enhance overall system usability. I am motivated by creating practical, user-focused technologies that serve communities, promote inclusivity, and improve access to essential information and services.

research-team.name: Janzzen Mitz Rogelle Cuentas
research-team.testimonial: I'm Janzzen Mitz Rogelle Cuentas, a junior web developer who enjoys building clean, responsive, and user-friendly websites. I work mainly with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and I'm continually improving my skills in React. I like turning ideas into simple, functional interfaces, paying attention to details like accessibility, performance, and maintainable code.

dost-pchrd.name: Engr. Timothy Jen Roxas
dost-pchrd.position: Project Manager, Digital and Frontier Technologies for Health, DOST-PCHRD
dost-pchrd.testimonial: HealthPH is the perfect introduction of state-of-the-art techniques of disease surveillance in the Philippines, made possible through artificial intelligence. The monitoring of social media posts in four (4) different languages makes it possible for a fast, reliable, and nationwide system for the early detection of respiratory diseases to be made.

dost-pchrd.name: Ms. Louise Sky Olaguer
dost-pchrd.position: Program Head, Digital and Frontier Technologies for Health DOST-PCHRD
dost-pchrd.testimonial: Through the commendable efforts of the HealthPH team, the creation of an inclusive and innovative disease monitoring tool for respiratory diseases is no longer a dream. By utlizing informal data sources such as social media, the early detection of respiratory diseases can now reach the farthest of the Philippine islands. Through data analytics, the government and LGUs can also provide timely intervention to prevent disease outbreaks and bring about a safer, healthier Philippines.
